scalars.scalar_value: Bachelor’s degree or the equivalent in Accounting, Finance or related discipline.
Three years of experience in an accounting, finance, or auditing position.

items.item_text: 01. All applicants are required to submit responses to the following supplemental questions. Your responses will provide information about your background and experience related to this position and will be used in the screening and selection process. Be concise yet specific and informative in your responses to these supplemental questions. "See resume," attachments or links will not be accepted as a substitute for your responses to the questions in the following boxes. Incomplete responses will not be considered. Please indicate below that you have read and understand these instructions. Options: Yes | No

02. I understand that my application will be considered incomplete if any required sections of the application are not completed and/or if any documents that are required are not attached to my online application by the closing date. Options: Yes | No
03. Please specify your highest level of education. Options: High School or equivalent (GED) | Associate's Degree | Bachelor's Degree | Master's Degree | Juris Doctor | Doctorate Degree
04. Please indicate the field in which you have earned your degree in:

05. Please indicate the number of years of experience you have in an accounting, finance, or auditing position. Options: No experience | One Year | Two Years | Three Years | Four Years | Five Years or more

06. Indicate where you have worked to obtain experience in an accounting, finance, or auditing What was the time frame? What was the employer's name? Describe the work performed. This section is required.
07. Do you have work experience in Higher Education? Options: Yes | No

08. Which best describes your experience performing complex accounting analysis and resolving discrepancies? Options: A. I have limited experience with complex accounting analysis or reconciliations. | B. I have performed routine reconciliations and resolved discrepancies using established procedures. | C. I independently analyze complex accounting issues, identify causes of discrepancies, and determine corrective actions. | D. I regularly lead complex accounting analyses, resolve significant discrepancies, and implement improvements to prevent recurring issues.

09. Which best describes your experience preparing and reviewing financial reports and financial statements? Options: A. I have limited experience preparing or reviewing financial reports. | B. I have assisted with routine financial reports and statements. | C. I independently prepare and review monthly, quarterly, or annual financial reports. | D. I prepare and analyze complex financial statements, reports, schedules, and supporting reconciliations for management or regulatory purposes.

10. Which best describes your experience with journal entries, budget revisions, expenditure transfers, and year-end accounting? Options: A. I have limited experience with these activities. | B. I have processed routine transactions using established procedures. | C. I independently prepare and review journal entries, budget changes, and year-end transactions. | D. I regularly review complex transactions, determine appropriate accounting treatment, and provide guidance regarding budget and year-end activities.

11. Which best describes your knowledge of California Community College accounting and fiscal requirements? Options: A. I have no experience with California Community College accounting requirements. | B. I have limited familiarity with California Community College fiscal requirements. | C. I have experience applying California Community College accounting and fiscal requirements in my work. | D. I have extensive experience interpreting and applying California Community College accounting requirements, including the Chancellor’s Office Budget and Accounting Manual.

12. Which best describes your experience with financial management systems and technology? Options: A. I have limited experience using financial management systems. | B. I regularly use financial systems to perform accounting functions. | C. I have participated in financial system testing, implementation, report development, or system upgrades. | D. I have served as a key accounting lead in financial system implementation, testing, data validation, reporting, or technology projects in collaboration with IT.

13. Which best describes your experience providing leadership, training, or technical guidance to accounting staff? Options: A. I have not provided formal accounting guidance or training to other staff. | B. I occasionally assist coworkers with accounting questions or procedures. | C. I regularly provide technical guidance, training, or coordination to accounting staff. | D. I lead accounting projects or teams, prioritize assignments, review work, establish deadlines, and provide advanced technical guidance and training.

14. Describe how you have demonstrated sensitivity and understanding in delivery of services and support to a diverse workforce and student population (diverse in terms of socioeconomic, cultural, disability, gender identity, sexual orientation, and ethnic background). This section is required.
Professional certification such as CPA, CMA, or CFE.
Bachelor’s degree or the equivalent in Accounting, Finance or related discipline.
Three years of experience in an accounting, finance, or auditing position.
Experience coordinating fiscal year-end processes, including balance rollovers and encumbrance adjustments.

Serve as the accounting lead, responsible for supporting the work of other accounting staff as directed by the supervisor (e.g., prioritizing projects, assisting with delegating assignments, setting deadlines, reviewing work, and providing training and accounting guidance); assist with planning and workflow for the department; coordinate staff in the analysis, completion, and validation of complex and technical projects; may lead department staff training.

Analyze, review, and interpret various information from Federal, State, County, District, and other relevant agencies, including accounting and financial reporting requirements, laws and regulations, policies and procedures, and other applicable guidance. Assist in the implementation of new governmental accounting standards.

Perform, analyze, research, and review advanced technical calculations, reconciliations, and complex accounting issues; identify causes of discrepancies and corrective measures, and implement necessary changes in processes or procedures.
Prepare or assist in the preparation of various monthly, quarterly, and annual reports and financial statements.

Review, provide recommendations, and process regular or recurring budget changes, transfers of expenditures, and journal entries for accuracy, completeness, proper authorization, and appropriate support. Review and process year-end entries.

Assist management in maintaining the chart of accounts, including, but not limited to, creating new funds, organizations, accounts, and program codes in accordance with the California Community Colleges Chancellor’s Office Budgeting and Accounting Manual and District policies and procedures.

Prepare and compile a variety of advanced and complex financial analyses, comprehensive reports and schedules, and reconciliations that require a degree of professional judgment, for management review and in compliance with District, State, Federal governmental, or other agencies’ requirements.

Monitor and maintain assigned financial activities and general ledger accounts for all District funds, ensuring the accuracy of the financial database. Monitor financial reporting deadlines. Review financial reports and data for accuracy, completeness, and appropriate support.

Perform ongoing analysis of general ledger accounts and appropriation ledger accounts. Respond to inquiries from external agencies, as assigned, such as the State Chancellor’s Office, Department of Education, other grant sponsors, auditors, and internal District staff. Coordinate information and communications among the District, campus departments, the County, and external agencies to clarify and reconcile expenditures, allocations, and accounting issues or inconsistencies.

Identify processes and procedures within Fiscal Services that need improvement, such as inefficiencies or gaps in internal controls. Provide recommendations using a District-wide approach. Implement or assist management in implementing process improvements and new technologies within Fiscal Services, such as creating or redesigning department procedures, documenting procedures or training manuals, developing or modifying financial systems and applications, and developing and testing new system-generated financial reports. Act as a core team member representing Fiscal Services and work collaboratively with IT and other departments as needed.

Lead IT projects for Fiscal Services; perform testing of financial management systems or emerging technologies to ensure the delivery of accurate, timely, and consistent, high-quality data; communicate changes and provide training. Perform general maintenance of financial systems and applications as directed and in collaboration with IT. Analyze and validate financial data.
Assist with the fiscal year-end close process in the District’s financial system, including rolling ending balances and encumbrances forward in the District’s financial system.
Reconcile bank accounts and the District’s detailed accounting records with the Los Angeles County Office of Education (LACOE) on a monthly basis.
Assist management with District-wide training on various fiscal affairs topics. Prepare and deliver presentations as needed.
Compile and develop necessary financial and narrative data in preparation for audits.
Participate in committees, task forces, and special assignments, including, but not limited to, screening and selection committees and mandated trainings, as required.
Perform related duties and responsibilities as required.
Proficiency in supervising and guiding accounting teams on complex fiscal projects and workflows.
Expertise in interpreting and applying State, Federal, and District financial regulations.
Aptitude for resolving advanced accounting discrepancies through in-depth analysis and process refinement.
Competence in evaluating and processing journal entries, budget revisions, and year-end financial activities.
Familiarity with maintaining and modifying the chart of accounts in compliance with regulatory guidelines.
Accuracy in monitoring financial systems for integrity, timeliness, and adherence to reporting deadlines.
Confidence in representing the department in communications with auditors, external agencies, and internal stakeholders.
Insight into assessing and improving accounting procedures and internal controls across fiscal operations.
Technical fluency in financial system testing, implementation, and maintenance in collaboration with IT.
Capacity to compile mandated financial reports (e.g., CCFS 311, IPEDS) in accordance with legal requirements.
Precision in reconciling financial records with external agencies such as LACOE and banking institutions.
Effectiveness in delivering training, presentations, and support on fiscal topics to diverse District stakeholders.
Advanced Technical Accounting Expertise
Regulatory Compliance & Policy Interpretation
Analytical Thinking & Problem Solving
Leadership & Staff Development
Process Improvement & Operational Efficiency
Project Management & Initiative
Ethical Judgment & Confidentiality
Capability to compile, interpret, and review detailed financial statements and periodic reports
Skill in producing high-level financial analysis and reconciliations requiring professional judgment.
Communication & Interpersonal Skills
